summary: SPA-in-deployment fix PARTIALLY VERIFIED. Local SPA serving works perfectly: GET / returns HTML with #root div (1214B), entry-bd7258f1b2479c1463b6fc81d9b5ec7f.js serves 200 (2.84MB), favicon.ico 200, /random-route falls back to index.html (SPA fallback OK), /api/health returns {status:ok}. Backend logs confirm 'Mounting Expo web build from /app/frontend/dist' — fallback branch does NOT trigger. Regression: 115/116 passed on first run; the 1 failure (test_login_worker_client_admin) was a transient network timeout to preview URL and passed on retry — full 116/116 effectively pass. HOWEVER: The .gitignore fix is INCOMPLETE. `git check-ignore frontend/dist/index.html` returns exit 1 (good, top-level files un-ignored), BUT 37 out of 41 files in frontend/dist/ are STILL git-ignored because the `node_modules/` rule (line 8) matches the intermediate path `frontend/dist/assets/node_modules/...` — this includes ALL icon fonts (FontAwesome, Feather, MaterialIcons, MaterialCommunityIcons, Ionicons, etc.) and expo-router bundled assets. After user redeploys, the HTML+JS will serve but icons/fonts will be BROKEN in production.

gitignore_issue.problem: 37 of 41 files in frontend/dist/ are still git-ignored due to `node_modules/` pattern in /app/.gitignore line 8 matching intermediate path `frontend/dist/assets/node_modules/...`
gitignore_issue.impact: Production redeploy will still be missing 90% of Expo bundled assets — vector-icon fonts, expo-router assets, react-navigation icons. SPA will load but visuals will break (missing icons/glyphs).
gitignore_issue.recommended_fix:
Add explicit whitelist for the nested path in /app/.gitignore, e.g.:
  !frontend/dist/assets/node_modules/
  !frontend/dist/assets/node_modules/**
OR globally: `!frontend/dist/` `!frontend/dist/**/*` placed AFTER the node_modules ignore lines (git patterns are order-sensitive but re-inclusion of files inside an ignored directory requires the parent dir to not be ignored — use `**` recursively).
gitignore_issue.verification_command: cd /app && find frontend/dist -type f | while read f; do git check-ignore "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo IGNORED || echo OK; done | sort | uniq -c

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix /app/.gitignore to also un-ignore frontend/dist/assets/node_modules/** so icon fonts and expo-router bundled assets get tracked. Verify by running: find frontend/dist -type f | xargs -I{} sh -c 'git check-ignore {} >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo OK {}' | wc -l — should equal 41.
After the .gitignore fix, git add /app/frontend/dist and commit before user redeploys.
critical_code_review_comments: .gitignore fix from this iteration only covered top-level dist files. The recursive node_modules/ ignore pattern at line 8 supersedes deep re-inclusion because gitignore cannot re-include files inside an already-ignored directory unless the containing directory chain is also re-included.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent fixes .gitignore for the nested node_modules path, re-run: 1) find frontend/dist -type f | while read f; do git check-ignore "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo IGNORED; done | wc -l — should be 0. 2) Re-run SPA smoke test (curl localhost:8001/). 3) Regression suite (test_phase1/2/3 + test_wallet_signs_iter13).
rca_of_issue: RCA: Original bug was root .gitignore had `dist/` blocking whole path. Iter14 fix added `!frontend/dist/` and `!frontend/dist/**` un-ignore. BUT git .gitignore semantics: `**` re-inclusion cannot un-ignore files inside a directory whose name matches an earlier ignore rule (e.g., `node_modules/`). Because the Expo web build places bundled assets under `frontend/dist/assets/node_modules/@expo/vector-icons/...`, the `node_modules/` rule on line 8 keeps 37/41 files ignored. Reproduction: `git check-ignore frontend/dist/assets/node_modules/@expo/vector-icons/build/vendor/react-native-vector-icons/Fonts/FontAwesome6_Regular.370dd5af19f8364907b6e2c41f45dbbf.ttf` → matches. Mitigation: Add explicit un-ignore for the nested path OR rename `node_modules/` rule to only match top-level using `/node_modules/` and remove line 8's `node_modules/`.
